newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech to amend FCC long-distance filing.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech to amend FCC long-distance filing.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Wednesday it will amend its filing with the Federal Communications Commission seeking approval to offer long-distance service from its local-calling region.

A spokesman for the Chicago-based Baby Bell also said it would ask the FCC to "restart the clock" on its filing after conceding certain documents were missing and would require amendments or substitutions.
Under last year's communications law, the agency has 90 days to approve or reject the bid.

Ameritech, in a filing of more than 4,000 pages with the FCC, asked on Jan. 2 for permission to offer long-distance service from Michigan, making it the first of the Baby Bells to seek approval for in-region long-distance service.

That would mean the FCC -- which must consult with Michigan regulators and the U.S. Justice Department -- would have to make a decision by April 2, according to the Ameritech spokesman. Michigan regulators must issue their recommendation by Jan. 22 and the Justice Department must do so by Feb. 6.
The Ameritech spokesman said the company now wants the FCC to push back the timetable until mid-April.
"We're talking a page here and a page there," the spokeesman said of the missing documents. "Our view is this is no big deal."

But the omissions are unlikely to help Ameritech in its case before the FCC and other regulators. The company passed up the opportunity to come in and consult with FCC officials for guidance before submitting its voluminous application.
Asked about whether the FCC would restart the clock, an FCC spokeswoman would say only: "We have an open proceeding. We'll have to wait till they file."

A source familiar with the filing said material is missing from the agreements Ameritech submitted to show it has opened its local network to rivals. That is the yardstick the FCC must use in determining whether to grant the carrier's bid.

In its initial press release, Ameritech said that Michigan regulators had approved the carrier's "interconnection" agreement with AT&T Corp that governs how AT&T will link up to Ameritech's local network.
But an AT&T spokesman said Wednesday the agreement is still pending before state regulators and the company has not yet heard from Michigan officials.
